html:
SMTO-FIL-0050 — SMTO couldn't keep a file's hidden details, so it didn't save it

GUID: 1923d0a4-4928-40f6-8bd9-9b0d7c84bdef
Slug: file-metadata-failed
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: fil

What happened

  • When SMTO copies or replaces a file, it keeps the file's hidden details, such as tags or security labels. That failed, so this file was not saved. Files finished earlier in the same request may already be in place.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you are saving to a USB stick or a shared network folder, try a folder on the computer's own disk instead. Some drives, such as many USB sticks, can't store these hidden file details at all.
  2. For a copy, if you don't need the hidden details kept, tell SMTO to copy the file without keeping its hidden details. SMTO only leaves these details behind when you ask it to.
  3. Before trying again, ask SMTO to list the destination folder. Files finished earlier in the same request may already be there, so you can avoid copying them twice.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the file as saved, and it appears in the destination folder.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; they include the computer's own error number. Don't open up permissions on whole folders just to make this pass.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Extended-attribute preservation raised OSError while preparing a staged file, so the stage was aborted and that file was not published.

What this means

  • Extended-attribute preservation raised OSError while preparing staged content, before that stage could be published. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Extended-attribute preservation raised OSError while preparing staged content, before that stage could be published.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect destination metadata support and permissions, while retaining receipts for any earlier items in a multi-item operation.

How to fix it

  • Check errno/winerror in the result and whether the destination filesystem supports the source's extended attributes (for example ENOTSUP on FAT/exFAT or some network shares, EPERM for protected attribute namespaces). Use a destination that supports them or grant the needed attribute permission; for file copy the caller may explicitly pass preserve_metadata=false, while replacement writes always preserve attributes.
  • Inspect the destination filesystem support and metadata permissions. Resolve the preservation failure before retrying; do not silently drop required metadata.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended staged item preserves required metadata and completes supported publication.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
